name: Agroforestry Regeneration Communities
imageAlt: Lush mixed planting at a Contour Lines agroforestry site in Guatemala
imageCaption: Contour Lines, Guatemala. Photograph shared by ARC.
summary: Smallholder farmers growing nourishing food and more resilient landscapes, one food forest at a time.
leader: A collective of smallholder farmers, agroforestry teachers, and local organizations
challenge: Smallholder farming communities face unpredictable weather, declining soil health, and barriers to training and resources. Food forests bring food production and ecosystem restoration together.
approach: Launched in April 2021, ARC connects farmers with regenerative agriculture and agroforestry education. Its model takes experienced teachers to communities, helping local people develop skills where they live and grow food.
support: AEF’s archived materials describe support for ARC through fundraising, grants for teachers, and connections across the regenerative agriculture community.
outcomeNote: Cumulative ARC figures reported on AEF’s 2025 website. These describe partner-network results, not outcomes attributable solely to AEF. The underlying reporting period was not specified.

name: Towards Green Environment
imageAlt: A scene from Towards Green Environment’s community work in Kenya
imageCaption: Towards Green Environment. From AEF’s archived project photography.
summary: Locally led responses to flooding, connecting children’s wellbeing, education, and a healthier environment.
leader: Towards Green Environment’s Kenyan environmentalists and volunteers
challenge: Flooding has disrupted life in Osodo Village. Families need immediate practical support as well as the knowledge and resources to adapt to a changing climate.
approach: The team combines environmental awareness, training, and community support. Its documented work includes food for children, menstrual products for women and girls, and mosquito nets to reduce malaria risk.
support: AEF’s archived homepage credits its support with helping TGE continue feeding children and providing essential supplies to the community.
outcomes: Food support for children in Osodo Village
Menstrual products supplied to women in the community
outcomeNote: Activities reported on the archived August 2025 homepage; quantities and needs have not been reverified for the current year.

name: Beyond Organic Design
imageAlt: Students observing growing plants in an Eco-Designers educational program
imageCaption: Educational work shared by Eco-Designers, the current name used by Beyond Organic Design. Photograph from eco-designers.com, reviewed September 2026.
summary: Helping young people become eco-literate designers of the world they will inherit.
leader: Beyond Organic Design’s educators and student community
challenge: Young people need practical ways to respond to environmental challenges, including in densely built urban places. Education can turn concern into confidence and useful skills.
approach: BOD’s Eco-Designers program brings permaculture design, hands-on learning, and educator development into schools. Its customizable curriculum connects environmental thinking with students’ everyday surroundings.
support: AEF featured BOD as a supported project and offered a dedicated fundraising pathway for its educational work.
outcomes: More than 6,165 young people reached by BOD’s courses
outcomeNote: BOD’s cumulative reach as reported on AEF’s 2025 homepage, rather than a count of students funded solely by AEF.

name: Youth in Permaculture Prize
imageAlt: Brenda Nakafeero, a 2022 Youth in Permaculture Prize recipient
summary: Recognizing young people bringing permaculture into gardens, classrooms, and their communities.
challenge: Young people have ideas and local knowledge, but often lack the funding and practical support to put them into action.
approach: The prize supported youth-led initiatives such as kitchen gardens, school learning spaces, native forests, and permaculture education. Archived recipient stories span 2018–2022.
support: AEF’s project directory describes financial awards to youth-led projects. Its archive preserves individual recipients’ plans and the purposes for which the awards were made.
outcomes: 23 youth-led projects in 15 countries, as reported in the project directory
Brenda Nakafeero’s kitchen-garden and learning-center plans in Uganda
School and community education projects across multiple regions
outcomeNote: Historical program reporting. Recipient plans are not presented as verified completed outcomes. No current prize round is advertised here.

name: Regenerative Holistic Resource Center
imageAlt: Agroforestry field learning photographed in ARC’s East African network
imageCaption: Related agroforestry training in ARC’s network; contextual photograph, not a verified RHRC event.
summary: Practical permaculture education that connects community wellbeing with regenerative food growing.
leader: Willis Orum and the Regenerative Holistic Resource Center
challenge: Communities need access to practical regenerative farming knowledge and support for vulnerable children and families.
approach: The center provides hands-on learning in syntropic agroforestry and permaculture, sharing techniques that participants can put to use in their own communities.
support: AEF’s project directory describes support for Willis Orum’s training work, and its donation page includes a dedicated pathway for the center.
outcomes: Hands-on community training described in AEF’s project directory
A dedicated fundraising pathway in the archived AEF website
outcomeNote: Historical description of activities. Current participant counts and program availability require an update from the project.

name: Refarmers · Grandmothers’ Kitchen Gardens
imageAlt: Food-growing work in the Refarmers network in Uganda
imageCaption: Refarmers, Uganda. Photograph shared by ARC.
summary: Using regenerative food growing to support nourishment, skills, and sustainable livelihoods.
challenge: Older people, mothers, and children can be particularly exposed to food insecurity. Gardens close to home offer one practical way to improve access to fresh food.
approach: The archived project story describes kitchen gardens in Kitgum and opportunities to share permaculture knowledge with young people and families.
support: AEF listed Refarmers among its supported projects and documented Ola Tom Lakere’s 2020 Youth in Permaculture Prize award connected to this work.
outcomes: Support for permaculture learning and youth knowledge-sharing
outcomeNote: A historical project profile drawn from AEF’s archive. No current funding target or beneficiary total is asserted.
